highlights.title: Sparking Dynamic, Relativistic Magnetic Reconnection in a Twisted Flux Tube
highlights.reason: 本文深入研究了磁星磁层细长扭缠磁通管中的相对论磁重联，结合非均匀电阻率与电荷匮乏机制，对解释磁星快速射电暴（FRB）前身辐射微结构、射电瞬变及巨耀斑重子抛射机制具有关键理论指导价值。

highlights.title: The transformative power of ALMA2040 for mm-VLBI
highlights.reason: 该白皮书评估了 ALMA2040 升级对毫米波甚长基线干涉测量（mm-VLBI）的赋能，大幅降低基线探测极限至 sub-mJy 水平，不仅可将黑洞阴影观测由个案扩展至小样本，还能在微角秒（$\mu\mathrm{as}$）尺度对 GRB、TDE、超新星及微类星体等高能瞬变源开展快速成像与相对论喷流物理诊断。

highlights.title: A New AI/ML Based Image Reconstruction Technique for Hard X-ray Coded Aperture Imagers
highlights.reason: 该研究针对 Swift BAT 等用于高能瞬变源（如 GRB 及致密天体爆发）监测的硬X射线编码孔径望远镜，提出了一种无需显式掩模反演的 CNN-Transformer 混合端到端成像算法，能在极低光子数和高背景噪声下实现高精度源定位，为未来非平面几何宽视场瞬变源探测仪器的星载实时成像提供了新方法。

highlights.title: A Unified Solution to the Low-Mass X-ray Binary Diversity Puzzle: Saturated Magnetic Braking Coupled with Irradiation-Driven Winds
highlights.reason: 文章针对低质量X射线双星（LMXB）演化中的观测质量转移率偏低、超紧凑双星（UCXB）形成参数精细调节以及毫秒脉冲星（MSP）轨道周期分布空缺等核心矛盾，提出了饱和磁制动结合辐照风（SMB+IDW）的物理模型，为致密天体高能观测与脉冲星双星演化提供了自洽的定量标度。

highlights.title: Gamma-ray calorimetry of Seyfert winds
highlights.reason: 文章构建了非喷流射电宁静塞弗特星系（Seyfert）超快外流（UFO）与激波强子加速的质子量能器（calorimetry）分析框架，定量对比了外流机械功率向GeV伽马射线的转化效率，与高能瞬变源的环境相互作用、激波强子加速及中微子/高能观测紧密相关。

highlights.title: What can a uniform reflection pipeline establish about supermassive black hole spin? An audit and a corrected analysis of 57 AGN with XMM and NuSTAR
highlights.reason: 该工作对致密天体高能观测中利用 XMM-Newton 与 NuSTAR 联合相对论 X 射线反射谱测定超大质量黑洞自旋 $a_*$ 的自动化流水线进行了系统审计与修正重算，发现背景漏扣和局部极小值等缺陷会导致误导性自旋限制，为致密天体高能能谱拟合提供了关键的可靠性检验。

highlights.title: Maximal efficiency of geometric beaming and polarization of highly super-Eddington X-ray sources
highlights.reason: 文章系统探究了超临界吸积流（ULX/PULX及高红移LRD等）漏斗状空腔中几何集束与X射线偏振的理论上限，证明多重散射光子沿漏斗边缘侧向逃逸使实际集束因子远低于纯几何极限$\mathcal{B}_{\rm max}=(1-\cos\alpha)^{-1}$，为致密天体超爱丁顿吸积、相对论外流准直及高能偏振观测提供了严格的定量基准。

highlights.title: Seeing Through the RFI Mask: DT-FISTA Inpainting of Pulsar Dynamic Spectra via Fourier Sparsity
highlights.reason: 脉冲星及 FRB 的动态谱与次级谱闪烁弧分析是探测星际与周围等离子体介质湍流结构的核心工具。论文针对射频干扰（RFI）切除掩模导致傅里叶次级谱严重泄漏、掩盖微弱闪烁弧（功率低于主信号 $10^{-3}$）的技术瓶颈，提出了计算复杂度仅为 $\mathcal{O}(KN\log N)$ 的递减阈值快速迭代收缩阈值算法（DT-FISTA），大幅超越传统稠密维纳滤波修复，为处理大视场、全分辨率致密天体闪烁数据提供了高精度低开销的数据处理工具。

highlights.title: Ranking Prompt--Plateau Correlations in Gamma-Ray Bursts with Symbolic Regression
highlights.reason: 该工作利用符号回归（PySR）算法在包含 251 个 GRB 样本中无约束搜索瞬时辐射与 X 射线平台相的经验关联，揭示了连接瞬时峰值光度与平台特征的三维经验平面，并排除了光度距离伪相关，为中心引擎持续供能与平台期物理机制提供了明确的定量约束。

highlights.title: The Dancing Bonfire: An Unusual Persistent X-ray Source in M81 Exhibiting Recurrent Luminous Flares
highlights.reason: 该工作基于 Chandra、XMM-Newton、Swift/XRT 与 NuSTAR 约 25 年的多空间望远镜观测，报道了 M81 中一个超亮持久 X 射线源 M81F4 表现出的快升慢衰复发性 X 射线耀斑，并深入论证了磁化中子星盘-磁层共转边界不稳定性（D'Angelo-Spruit RII 不稳定性）驱动超爱丁顿吸积的物理机制，对致密天体极端吸积与瞬变物理具有直接参考价值。

highlights.title: A blazar is a blazar is a blazar ... Comparing long-term varaibility properties of PKS 1510-089 and PKS 2155-304
highlights.reason: 该工作利用 Swift 与 Fermi 近 20 年的多波段数据，对比了平谱射电类星体（FSRQ）与高频峰 BL Lac（HBL）两类典型耀变体的长时标光变、互相关及通量分布，对相对论喷流的多区与分层辐射机制研究具有参考价值。

highlights.title: Three-dimensional spatial modelling of nuclear de-excitation lines
highlights.reason: 论文通过结合 GALPROP 3D 宇宙线输运与 TALYS 核反应截面，系统模拟了银河系低能宇宙线（LECR）引发的原子核退激发 MeV 伽马射线发射（如 4.4 MeV、6.1 MeV 和 1.6 MeV）。研究对银心区域高电离率所需的宇宙线能量预算进行了定量限制，指出其所需的注入功率远超超新星遗迹（SNR）的常规加速能力，对致密天体环境、高能粒子加速与 MeV 伽马射线观测（如 COSI）具有参考价值。

highlights.title: Prospects for Simultaneously Detecting Long and Short Duration Gravitational Waves from Pulsar Glitches with Current and Future Detectors
highlights.reason: 文章系统量化了当前与第三代（3G）地面引力波网络协同探测脉冲星自转突变（glitch）时长时标瞬态连续波（tCW，瞬态山）与短时标爆发（f-mode 阻尼振荡）的灵敏度，明确指出了双重探测瓶颈在于高频 burst 搜寻及天区位置依赖，对致密天体多信使引力波搜寻与中子星物态方程限制具有明确的参考价值。

highlights.title: Exploring Cosmic Rays from Gravity-Limited Acceleration at Supermassive Black Holes
highlights.reason: 文章探讨了超大质量黑洞（SMBH）视界尺度引力限制磁场加速超高能宇宙线（UHECR）的理论机制，并利用皮埃尔·奥格天文台（PAO）观测数据检验了宁静态星系核与 AGN 的空间角相关性，与高能粒子加速及致密天体环境直接相关。

highlights.title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
highlights.reason: 文章系统量化了双中子星并合（NSM）及其吸积盘外流中，快中子俘获反应（n, gamma）统计模型输入（核能级密度 NLD 与 gamma 强度函数 GSF）对 r-过程核合成丰度的理论不确定度传播，与千新星中心引擎后光度及致密天体抛射物环境密切相关。

highlights.title: SN 2025wiu: A Type Ib Supernova with Post-Peak Optical Rebrightening
highlights.reason: 该工作报道了一例罕见的具有峰后光学再次增亮特征的 Type Ib 超新星 SN 2025wiu，详细分析了双峰光学光变、全波段热光度演化以及光谱特征，并对中心引擎（磁星/吸积）与非球对称 CSM 相互作用等能量机制进行了深入甄别，对研究剥层超新星（SESN）晚期能量注入及隐藏星周环境具有参考价值。

highlights.title: ExHaLe-jet: Modeling blazar jets with an extended hadro-leptonic radiation code
highlights.reason: 本文应用扩展动力学辐射代码 ExHaLe-jet 模拟耀变体相对论喷流全尺度空间演化，自洽求解强子与轻子含时输运及多信使辐射（光子与高能中微子），符合研究组对相对论喷流、多信使辐射机制及中心引擎能量耗散的研究关注。

highlights.title: Andreev Beta Conversion and Bulk Viscosity in Superfluid Neutron-Star Matter
highlights.reason: 论文通过非平衡场论提出了超流中子凝聚体与正常相粒子共存时的 Andreev 贝塔转换新通道，揭示了极低温下弱相互作用弛豫率从指数压低转变为幂律温控行为，为超新星残骸致密天体冷却、中子星并合震荡阻尼及中微子辐射物理提供了微观理论修正。

highlights.title: A precessing AGN with S-shaped morphology discovered in MALS
highlights.reason: 利用MeerKAT的高灵敏度低频射电巡天发现了一例典型S型进动喷流射电星系J1221$-$1354，通过射电谱老化分析和弹道进动喷流模型限制了相对论喷流运动学参量，为致密双黑洞（SMBHB）驱动喷流进动的物理图景提供了定量观测约束。

highlights.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
highlights.reason: 文章系统对比了具有早期闪光光谱（flash-spectroscopy，指示致密CSM相互作用）与无闪光特征的II型超新星的大样本（86例）多波段测光与颜色演化。提出了利用早期颜色拐折斜率变化 $\Delta cs$ 结合峰值绝对星等 $M_{\mathrm{peak}}$ 诊断致密星周介质相互作用的测光判据，并给出了闪光特征持续时间 $t_{\mathrm{IIn}}$ 与测光极小值相位 $t_{\mathrm{min}}$、转折相位 $t_{\mathrm{break}}$ 之间的关键定量时序约束 $t_{\mathrm{min}} \le t_{\mathrm{IIn}} < t_{\mathrm{break}}$。

entries.title: Modeling extreme mass-ratio inspirals in astrophysical and dark-matter environments
entries.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals offer a powerful probe of massive black holes and their environments, but interpreting their signals requires accurate models of orbital dynamics and radiation. Here we bring together advances in black-hole perturbation theory to establish a unified relativistic framework for adiabatic inspirals in perturbative astrophysical environments. Built on the modified Teukolsky formalism, the framework requires neither post-Newtonian nor slow-rotation approximations. As a first application, we calculate the leading cloud-induced corrections to gravitational-wave fluxes and conservative orbital dynamics for circular, equatorial inspirals around a rotating black hole surrounded by a synchronized ultralight scalar cloud, combining these corrections with the previously calculated scalar response. In our fiducial system, a cloud containing $10^{-4}$ of the black-hole mass produces about $-57.3$ radians of orbital dephasing over two years. The phase contributions from gravitational-wave flux corrections and background-induced orbital shifts each exceed the scalar contribution in magnitude and partially cancel, highlighting the need for coupled matter-gravity modeling. Extensible to other environments and modified gravity theories, our framework provides the relativistic inputs needed to assess detection losses and parameter biases, and to probe the nature of black-hole environments with future space-based gravitational-wave observations.

entries.title: Hidden Disruption in Milky Way-like Satellite Galaxy Populations
entries.abstract: Determining whether a satellite galaxy is tidally disrupting from photometric observations alone remains a fundamental challenge in near-field cosmology. Cosmological simulations of Milky Way-mass galaxies predict that satellite populations should be highly disrupted, yet the observed Milky Way satellite population appears largely intact. Understanding this tension requires either uncovering disruption that has gone undetected in Milky Way satellites, or identifying limitations in the simulations themselves. We use the Auriga suite of cosmological simulations to evaluate several commonly used indicators of disruption. We find that, in the simulated satellite population, the shape, size, and proper motion alignment of a satellite's bound component are unreliable indicators of its present-day disruption state despite their widespread use in the literature. In contrast, the extended stellar distribution, specifically the ratio of stellar mass between $3r_{1/2}$ and $10r_{1/2}$ to that within $r_{1/2}$, is strongly correlated with disruption. We introduce the extended mass ratio $μ_{\rm EMR}$ as a metric for comparing extended stellar distributions across satellites of varying masses and exploring their connection to disruption in Milky Way observations. Applying this metric to a sample of Milky Way satellites with measured extended stellar distributions, we find that many are consistent with significant ongoing disruption, even among systems traditionally classified as intact. These results suggest that tidal disruption may be substantially more widespread in the observed Milky Way satellite population than currently recognized, and establish extended stellar distributions as a promising new tool for uncovering this hidden disruption.

entries.title: The bar-driven central complex of NGC 6946: A panchromatic and spatially resolved view of its star formation history and interstellar medium
entries.abstract: We present a multi-wavelength analysis of the nearby spiral galaxy NGC 6946, combining optical IFS, infrared, and radio observations. We aim to characterise both the integrated and spatially resolved properties of the stellar populations and ISM, and to interpret them in the context of bar-driven galaxy evolution. We used the SED fitting code SINOPSIS to derive stellar population properties, and different prescriptions to derive ISM properties including atomic and molecular gas masses and the dust mass,temperature, and emissivity index. We find that the central 2.6 kpc hosts $40\%$ of the stellar mass, as well as the bulk of the molecular gas and dust, and has sustained enhanced star formation over cosmic time. A major star formation episode occurred 0.6 Gyr ago. The spatially resolved KS relation shows that molecular gas alone explains only part of the current SFR variance, while alternative prescriptions incorporating stellar mass and dynamical equilibrium pressure yield only modest improvements. We also find radial enhancements in the effective oxygen yield and gas mass fraction relative to surrounding regions, consistent with sustained gas accumulation. Together with the molecular gas streaming motions previously detected kinematic studies, our results are consistent with, and provide independent support for, the inward transport of gas driven by a system of nested bars and with a scenario in which a recent episode of bar-driven gas inflow enhanced the central molecular gas reservoir and sustained elevated star formation. These findings point to efficient HI-to-H$_2$ conversion, likely promoted by the combined effect of the secondary bar and the large dust content, ultimately regulating star formation. We also find indications consistent with a young stellar bar. The current decline in star formation despite large gas reservoirs suggests recent bar-driven quenching.

entries.title: Four Which I Knew Not: The Hexadecapole Nearly Cancels the Octupole in Librating Kozai-Lidov Cycles
entries.abstract: Phenomena requiring close proximity between two bodies, from black-hole mergers to hot Jupiters, may originate in hierarchical triples, in which secular torques from a distant companion drive the inner binary's eccentricity nearly to unity. Population syntheses of these channels commonly integrate the double-averaged (DA) secular equations truncated at octupole order. We show that, for a fixed outer orbit, this truncation fails for the slow evolution on librating Kozai-Lidov cycles, in which the argument of pericenter librates. On these cycles the leading octupole kicks to $j_z$, the component of the inner angular momentum along the outer one, cancel pairwise, and the hexadecapole enters at the order of the surviving octupole torque, with the opposite sign. Strikingly, as the inner mass ratio vanishes the two nearly cancel, and their sum changes sign within the librating window, so octupole-truncated integrations omit part of the leading slow torque on this class. For $|j_z|\ll1$, the slow dynamics driven by the hexadecapole is approximately solved analytically as a simple pendulum in the doubled azimuth of the eccentricity vector, with closed-form coefficients on rotating and librating cycles. For a circular outer orbit the hexadecapole-modified cycles are solved exactly. For unequal inner masses the octupole adds to the pendulum's torque on librating cycles, where its alternating kick can also flip orbits, and generally dominates rotating ones. DA integrations follow the predicted excursions, periods and flip criteria. Population consequences depend on the validity of the high-eccentricity reduction and on other processes affecting the cycles.

entries.title: Contrasting geometries of kiloparsec-scale stellar flows associated with giant Galactic cavities
entries.abstract: Giant bubbles and cavities are widespread in star-forming galactic discs, yet the stellar dynamics associated with such structures remain poorly constrained. Here we combine Gaia Data Release 3 with three-dimensional extinction information to identify 3,502 massive-star candidates corresponding to initial masses $M_{\rm ini}\gtrsim8\,M_{\odot}$ within 5 kpc of the Sun. A search of the stellar-density field alone, independent of interstellar-medium morphology and stellar kinematics, reveals two prominent overdensities, R1 and R2, with characteristic scales of approximately 1.3 kpc. Both are subsequently found to be associated with previously identified giant interstellar cavities in projected position and line-of-sight location. After subtracting locally fitted background velocity fields, stars with full three-dimensional velocities reveal coherent divergent in-plane motions across both structures. R1 extends well beyond a known massive-star association and exhibits strongly anisotropic expansion, with one principal strain rate robustly positive and the other consistent with zero. R2 instead exhibits positive strain rates along both principal directions, indicating broadly two-dimensional internal expansion. These results show that density-selected, cavity-associated stellar structures of comparable scale can host coherent kiloparsec-scale flows with contrasting internal flow geometries and need not share a common stellar kinematic organisation.

entries.title: Let Sleeping Stars Li: Mapping Turnoff Lithium, the Lithium Dip, & Testing Standard Model Predictions in GALAH DR4 Subgiants
entries.abstract: Lithium is an excellent tracer of stellar mixing. We reconstruct the end of the main sequence lithium depletion pattern using the GALAH DR4 3D-NLTE lithium dataset for 22,442 stars, complemented by masses and subgiant lithium dilution factors inferred from YREC stellar models. We recover the two canonical features seen in clusters: a cool plateau ($\mathrm{M_{[Fe/H]_{\odot}}} \sim 1.2 \mathrm{M_\odot}$) with a median $A(Li) = 2.42$, and a steep plunge into the lithium dip ($\mathrm{M_{[Fe/H]_{\odot}}} \sim 1.35 \mathrm{M_\odot}$) dominated by upper limits at $A(Li) < 1.5$. Above the dip, our data reveal a striking new pattern with a wide range of abundances. We argue this reflects severe rotationally induced mixing in most stars, with lithium preserved in a minority where gravitational settling suppresses mixing. Lithium depletion with intrinsic dispersion is universal across the sample. Predicted and observed dilution trends agree well below the dip. For higher-mass stars, dilution corrections agree with standard models, but our upper envelope lies below open cluster values. We attribute this to a shallower lithium preservation zone and further evidence for gravitational settling and radiative levitation. We detect lithium in $\approx25\%$ of dip stars, whereas clusters show none; neither blurring of a narrow mass feature nor binary contamination fully explains this. The cool plateau is 0.8 dex below the solar meteoritic value across a wide range of $[Fe/H]$. After accounting for pre-main sequence depletion, the plateau is elevated at $\geq [Fe/H]_{\odot}$, possibly evidence for lithium production.

entries.title: Constraints on Decaying Dark Matter with $B=1$ from Fermi-LAT
entries.abstract: We investigate the gamma ray signatures of fermionic dark matter that carries one unit of baryon number and decays into three quarks. We compute the expected prompt and secondary gamma-ray spectra for a representative range of final state flavor combinations. By comparing these spectra to Fermi-LAT measurements of the isotropic gamma-ray background, we derive exclusion limits on the lifetime. We observe that depending on the dark matter mass and the flavor of the final state, the lifetime bounds on decays of $B=1$ dark matter can differ by up to a factor of two from those on decays of $B=0$ dark matter. Furthermore, light-quark final states generally yield stronger bounds at lower masses, whereas heavy-quark final states can yield comparable or stronger bounds at masses of tens of TeV and above.

entries.title: Searching for Dwarf Novae in 47 Tucanae
entries.abstract: The globular cluster 47 Tucanae has 43 strong cataclysmic variable candidates, four of which are confirmed dwarf novae. Tidal capture theory predicts the existence of dozens of dwarf novae, suggesting more are undiscovered. Using 435 nm and 475 nm long exposure images from Hubble's ACS camera, we searched five epochs of archival Hubble images and did not find any variability at the scale of a dwarf nova eruption. We found 1 previously undiscovered variable object on the main sequence that could not be classified as a CV; the object experienced a change of approximately 0.3 Mag in 425 nm, and 0.2 mag in 635 nm over the course of 12 days. The lack of new CV detections in 47 Tucanae could be a result of the short timescale of the DN eruption, and a low observing probability. However, this null result may also support research suggesting most CVs in globular clusters are not dynamically formed, and tidal capture theory overestimates the detectable CV population.

entries.title: The Magnetized Universe: From planet-forming disks to the high-redshift universe
entries.abstract: The interstellar medium (ISM) is magnetized at all scales and phases in our Galaxy and other galaxies across the Universe. Spectro-polarimetric millimetre observations are essential to probe the role of the interstellar magnetic fields in the dynamics of the cold universe, and how this affects the star formation process, and planet formation in nearby star forming regions. Such observations are also essential for understanding magnetic fields in active stars and the shaping and evolution of the circumstellar environments of evolved stars. While ALMA has been revolutionary in advancing our knowledge about magnetic fields in the ISM, the limitations in calibration, especially for circular polarization, and sensitivity for large samples, have hindered robust measurements of field strengths, which are essential for fully assessing their role in ISM dynamics. An ALMA2040 that broadens spectro-polarimetric capabilities to include robust circular calibration and increases sensitivity with more collecting area will enable crucial observations of magnetic fields across the Universe and over a wide range of spatial scales to fully ascertain the influences of magnetic fields from galaxy assembly to forming planets.

entries.title: Sparking Dynamic, Relativistic Magnetic Reconnection in a Twisted Flux Tube
entries.abstract: Magnetic reconnection around neutron stars (NSs) forms small-scale currents while transferring energy to electron-positron pairs. These dissipating currents cover a wide range of scales, potentially leaving an imprint on time-variable X-ray bursts and pulsed radio emission. We present a reduced, planar model of internal reconnection in a magnetic flux tube with relativistic magnetization, finite resistivity, and strong guide field. Comparing with realistic NS parameters, this model represents the dynamics of a slender magnetic flux tube that is much thinner than the stellar radius. The seed current profile is smooth and does not spontaneously reconnect; instead, a discrete and localized current perturbation is introduced, representing e.g. localized energy release from a NS crust or magnetosphere. Three high-resolution relativistic magnetohydrodynamics simulations are described: one has uniform resistivity and Lundquist number such that reconnection proceeds in the plasmoid-mediated regime; the other two account for the feedback of charge starvation on the resistivity in current layers, where density is depleted; we provide a more general explanation for this depletion. All simulations produce a few dominant magnetic X-points and a secondary Kelvin-Helmholtz instability that excites high-wavenumber currents. We quantify the reconnection rate, the intermittency of dissipation, and the time profile of current spikes. We further present three-dimensional simulations confirming a limited growth of the ideal kink mode in the strong guide field regime. Applications are discussed, including to radio pulse microstructure and current damping below the magnetar surface during an X-ray flare, leading to mass loss and X-ray afterglow.

entries.title: The transformative power of ALMA2040 for mm-VLBI
entries.abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has resolved horizon-scale emission in M87* and Sgr A*. Extending these observations to fainter black holes, multiple frequencies, and evolving structures requires greater sensitivity and new observing capabilities. We investigate how ALMA2040 could expand the scientific reach of global millimeter very long baseline interferometry (mm-VLBI), compared with ALMA's Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade (WSU). Phasing a larger ALMA array and enabling simultaneous observations across multiple ALMA bands would improve sensitivity and frequency phase transfer, providing spectral and polarimetric diagnostics of gravity, accretion flows, magnetic fields, and relativistic jets. In the configurations studied, ALMA2040 achieves sub-mJy baseline sensitivity at 230 GHz and improves prospects for faint-source imaging at 345 GHz, opening a path from individual horizon-scale targets toward population studies. Simulated observations of M87* show improved multi-frequency recovery of emission from the compact ring-like region toward the jet base, enabling studies of the accretion-jet connection. For Sgr A*, simulations of interstellar scattering mitigation yield a 27% reduction in the error of the recovered intrinsic source structure relative to the WSU configuration. Beyond black holes, these capabilities benefit geometric-distance measurements, stellar masers, compact transients, and other applications of high-resolution astrophysics. Together with rapid-response capabilities across the VLBI network, ALMA2040 could support a transition from isolated snapshots toward multi-frequency, time-resolved studies of compact sources.

entries.title: Double Trouble: How Unresolved Spectroscopic Binary Stars Skew GALAH DR4 Stellar Parameters
entries.abstract: Unresolved binary stars introduce systematic biases in stellar parameter estimates when analysed assuming a single star. Using $\sim$917{,}000 spectra from the Galactic Archaeology with HERMES (GALAH) Data Release 4 (DR4), we develop a binary spectral model that fits each observed spectrum as the superposition of two synthetic spectra generated from the same model architecture used by GALAH DR4. These generative spectral models take as input: effective temperature ($T_\mathrm{eff}$), surface gravity ($\log g$), iron abundance ([Fe/H]), projected rotation velocity ($v \sin i$), microturbulence velocity ($v_\mathrm{mic}$), and radial velocity ($v_\mathrm{rad}$). In our binary model, $T_\mathrm{eff}$ and $\log g$ are not fitted directly but are instead interpolated from PARSEC isochrones based on stellar mass and age, under the assumption that both components formed contemporaneously with the same compositions. We fit for the primary and secondary masses, a common age and [Fe/H], as well as individual $v \sin i$, $v_\mathrm{mic}$, and $v_\mathrm{rad}$ for each component. After iterative optimization and conservative quality cuts to ensure robust detections, we identify $\sim$12{,}911 candidate binary systems. We quantify typical biases introduced by unresolved binarity: $T_\mathrm{eff}$ shifts of $-142$ to $+200$ K, $\log g$ shifts of $-0.070$ to $+0.35$ dex, and [Fe/H] shifts of $-0.055$ to $+0.13$ dex. Despite our conservative approach reducing the number of detections, we recover known trends of increasing binary fraction with higher primary mass and lower metallicity, thus reflecting the broad trends of binary populations. Accounting for unresolved binaries is essential for accurate stellar population modelling and for interpreting spectroscopic surveys--particularly in low-metallicity systems or populations with more massive stars.

entries.title: A New AI/ML Based Image Reconstruction Technique for Hard X-ray Coded Aperture Imagers
entries.abstract: Here we demonstrate a new AI/ML based image reconstruction method for coded-aperture instruments that provides a pathway for embedded real-time use on-board spaceflight missions. Using the Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) for our initial simulated demonstration, we used our new technique to replace the standard Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) based image reconstruction pipeline. In our alternative approach, we have created a neural network that maps detector counts directly to source positions using simulated responses from selected Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) observations. The network combines convolutional feature extraction with attention and is trained at around 900 source counts. Under zero background noise, it achieves over 93\% exact-pixel localization accuracy with 400 detected source photons. The model maintains at least 90\% exact-pixel localization accuracy with up to 8{,}500 added background counts for sources with 900 detected photons. Within the evaluated region of BAT's field of view, these results show that source position can be recovered from sparse coded-aperture measurements in a wide-field instrument. A key feature of this technique is that explicit inclusion of the mask pattern is not required. This allows us to train the algorithm to "see" using data accumulated from an imaging system. These new non-traditional imaging techniques show substantial promise in enabling efficient imaging using non-planar geometries, which will enable new classes of hard X/$γ$-ray imaging systems and simultaneously improve imaging capability for currently operating instruments.

entries.title: Pair-exchange dynamics of magnetohydrodynamic turbulence
entries.abstract: Nonlinear interactions in incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) and Navier-Stokes turbulence involve three spatial fluctuations conservatively exchanging, e.g., energy. The mathematical structure of a triad interaction does not allow to unambigously determine the specific contribution of each of the participating fluctuations to the resulting exchanges. Presently, only additional assumptions allow for the deconstruction of triad interactions into a sum of pair exchanges. This work proves that in incompressible MHD the simultaneous nonlinear transfer of cross-helicity sufficiently constrains the triad dynamics such that a mathematically unique pair-exchange representation of nonlinear energy and cross-helicity transfer is possible.

entries.title: Dust in Galaxies at $z=10-15$: Attenuation and Re-emission Predictions from the FirstLight Simulations
entries.abstract: Dust masses and grain properties in $z>10$ galaxies remain poorly constrained, as JWST UV attenuation and ALMA dust re-emission are rarely modelled consistently. We perform post-processed 3D dust radiative transfer on 208 snapshots of 99 galaxies at $z=10$-15 from the FirstLight simulations ($M_*=10^{6.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$), applying twelve dust models per snapshot (2496 runs): four dust-to-metal (DTM) prescriptions and three grain size distributions. Metallicity-dependent DTM models reproduce ALMA dust-mass upper limits at $z\gtrsim10$ and detections at $z\sim7$, as dust-to-stellar mass ratios rise sharply near $Z\sim0.2\,Z_\odot$, typically at $M_*\gtrsim10^{8.5}\,M_\odot$, where grain growth by metal accretion becomes dominant. A constant DTM of 0.4 instead violates more than half of the upper limits. For dust attenuation, SMC-like dust is favored by the observed $M_{\rm UV}$-$β_{\rm UV}$ relation. The observed UV slopes ($β_{\rm UV}\simeq-2.3$) favor small grains ($a\lesssimλ_{\rm UV}/2π\simeq0.025\,μ{\rm m}$) producing steep UV extinction, together with a low abundance of carbonaceous grains or PAHs responsible for the 2175 $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ bump, consistent with silicate-rich dust. Large-grain stellar dust ($a_0=0.1\,μ{\rm m}$) instead yields nearly grey extinction and UV slopes close to the intrinsic value ($β_{\rm UV,0}\simeq-2.6$). SMC and MW attenuation curves flatten at $A_{\rm V}\gtrsim0.3$, showing that relatively flat attenuation does not necessarily imply large grains. For dust re-emission, dust peak temperatures reach 60-80 K, exceeding the 40-50 K commonly assumed in ALMA dust-mass estimates. Predicted IR continuum flux increases with UV luminosity; at current ALMA sensitivities (10-20 $μ$Jy), detections generally require $M_{\rm UV}\lesssim-21.5$. Roman wide-field surveys may identify such rare UV-bright galaxies.

entries.title: A Multiwavelength View of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5: an X-ray Luminous and Eclipsing Dwarf Nova
entries.abstract: We report the independent discovery of the cataclysmic variable (CV) SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 using Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey 12 band photometry, following its initial identification via ASAS-SN variability. Here, we investigate the system using optical photometry alongside optical and X-ray spectroscopy. High-cadence optical light curves from publicly available TESS data and a dedicated campaign at the Pico dos Dias Observatory in Brazil revealed a highly inclined system exhibiting pronounced eclipses with an orbital period of 1.81 hours. We found no evidence of a WD spin period. Despite seasonal gaps, the long-term ASAS-SN light curve revealed several outbursts (15 with $Δ$mag $\sim$ 1.5 brighter than the mean magnitude) and one superoutburst over the past decade. During Swift X-ray telescope observations, the system exhibited X-ray luminosity of $8.5 \times 10^{31}$ erg s$^{-1}$ in the 0.3-10\,keV band, originating from thermal plasma emission at a temperature consistent with accretion shocks. Optical spectroscopy from the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrographs on the Gemini South telescope confirms the CV nature of the system, showing strong, double-peaked H and HeI emission lines alongside a weak HeII4686 line. Altogether, these features strongly support the classification of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 as a quiescent, eclipsing dwarf nova with an unusually high X-ray luminosity.

entries.title: Gaia in Technicolor. I. A Simple Variability-Encoded Color-Magnitude Diagram
entries.abstract: The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is one of the most important tools in stellar astrophysics. In its modern, empirical form as the Gaia color-magnitude diagram (CMD), each star is represented with a point determined from its time-averaged brightness and color. However, many stars are intrinsically variable, and the fixed-point representation ignores the variety of ways in which a star can vary. As a system pulsates, eclipses, is irradiated, erupts, or otherwise varies, it moves through the CMD along a trajectory whose size, slope, and shape are determined by the physics driving the brightness and color variability. Here we exploit the near-simultaneous, three-band, multi-epoch photometry (MEP) released for ~11.7 million sources in Gaia DR3 to construct a variability-encoded CMD (VECMD). In this updated take on the traditional CMD, each star is represented not by a point but by a linear segment approximating the path it traces in absolute magnitude and color as it varies. Because these trajectories are built from the raw epoch data, they are agnostic to period and do not require phase-folding. We show that radial-mode pulsators trace looped, Lissajous-like trajectories that can encode the phase lag between radius and temperature. The Hertzsprung bump is even visible in the CMD loops of some Cepheids. Variable binary systems can trace tight color-correlated lines and/or hooked paths. Accreting and dust-obscured systems trace long, high-amplitude tracks aligned with the outburst or reddening vector. Distinct regions of the VECMD are dominated by distinct trajectory morphologies. We argue that these trajectories are period-independent fingerprints well suited to machine learning classification, which we will pursue on the much larger epoch-photometry sample expected in Gaia DR4. Finally, we present a free app called IVECMD for finding, classifying, and analyzing variable stars in the VECMD.

entries.title: A Unified Solution to the Low-Mass X-ray Binary Diversity Puzzle: Saturated Magnetic Braking Coupled with Irradiation-Driven Winds
entries.abstract: The standard magnetic braking (MB) model has long failed to explain key properties of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs)---including their accretion rates, the formation of ultracompact binaries, and orbital expansion---casting doubt on binary evolution and gravitational-wave progenitor predictions. Phenomenological modifications exist, but a unified, physically grounded mechanism has been missing. Here we show that the overlooked coupling between magnetic saturation and irradiation-driven winds (IDW) provides this missing framework. Accretion-powered irradiation enhances the donor wind, which in turn amplifies MB exactly where needed. Our Saturated MB + IDW (SMB+IDW) model simultaneously resolves three outstanding discrepancies with no fine-tuning: (1) it reproduces the full observed distribution of accretion rates across persistent and transient LMXBs; (2) it naturally explains ultracompact X-ray binary formation; and (3) it quantitatively matches the orbital period distribution of descendant millisecond pulsar (MSP) binaries---a critical independent test failed by all previous models. Critically, the SMB+IDW model transforms MB from an externally imposed condition into a self-consistently regulated process tied to the accretion history. By unifying LMXB evolution to MSPs in a single physical picture, our work resolves the long-standing diversity puzzle and establishes a physics-based foundation for next-generation population synthesis, gravitational-wave progenitor predictions, and compact binary interpretation across cosmic time.

entries.title: Analytic and numerical study of dark matter halos in the Horndeski theory
entries.abstract: The models of modified gravity that can explain the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe must pass the local tests of gravity, introducing a screening mechanism so that any additional fifth force in gravity is suppressed at stellar scales. Dark matter halos, in contrast, by their extendedness in scale, may exhibit a transition of screening to small scales, providing a probe of modified gravity and the origin of the late-time acceleration. We perform comprehensive studies of dark matter halos with Vainshtein screening in the Horndeski theory. Given that dark matter is cold and a dark matter halo is spherically symmetric, we analytically clarify the conditions for the halo profile under which the Vainshtein screening works effectively. We find that the Vainshtein screening is less effective even within the Vainshtein radius as the profile approaches a core-like structure around the center of a halo, which motivates us to postulate that some features owing to the fifth force can survive during the dynamical evolution of a halo. We numerically examine our postulate by a $N$-body simulation for an isolated halo with the assumption of Newtonian two-body interactions with the spherical external fifth force. We make use of three proxies of the mass through hydrostatic dynamics, the Jeans equation, and gravitational lensing, all of which must be identical in the case of Newtonian gravity as a weak-field approximation to General Relativity. We find that these proxies can be biased relative to each other at a (quasi) equilibrium, quantitatively indicating that the fiducial model of gravity is not Newtonian. Our result affirmatively suggests that multiple mass proxies from observations are capable of testing gravity on halo scales.

entries.title: MIDSSAR: MId Dispersion Spectrograph for Stellar Activity Research
entries.abstract: We have developed and commissioned MIDSSAR (MId Dispersion Spectrograph for Stellar Activity Research), a novel fiber-fed, dual-band spectrograph optimized for high-cadence monitoring of stellar superflares and magnetic activity phenomena, mounted on the 3.8-m Seimei Telescope at Kyoto University Okayama Observatory. Utilizing a custom-designed volume phase holographic grating and a commercially available volume binary transmission grating, the instrument achieves simultaneous observations of key chromospheric activity indicators: the CaII H&K band (382.5-406.5nm) at a resolving power of R=13,800, and the H$α$ band (641.1-667.6nm) at R=18,200. MIDSSAR is strategically integrated with the existing high-dispersion spectrograph GAOES-RV to enable concurrent photosphere-chromosphere monitoring. The control software coordinates high-speed dual-camera exposures down to 1ms while incorporating real-time telescope telemetry into the data headers. We also developed a dedicated data reduction pipeline that automatically executes calibration, spatial reconstruction of the 61-fiber bundle, and one-dimensional spectral extraction with a wavelength precision of $\sim$ 0.002nm. Initial on-sky test observations conducted from March to May 2026 successfully verified the system's quantitative readiness. The observed signal-to-noise ratio characteristics perfectly align with modeled theoretical limits under varying seeing conditions, confirming that the entire instrument complex successfully meets its primary design requirements and operational expectations for systematic stellar astrophysics surveys.

entries.title: $\texttt{GASTRO-BH}$: Effects of a Central Black Hole in GSE-like Dwarf-galaxy Mergers Around Milky Way-like Hosts
entries.abstract: Recent evidence points to an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) in the most massive globular cluster of the Milky Way, $ω$ Centauri. This globular cluster is commonly associated with the Gaia-Sausage/Enceladus (GSE) dwarf galaxy, the last major merger event of our Galaxy, as its nuclear star cluster remnant. Motivated by this, we investigate whether the interaction between a bright GSE-like dwarf galaxy with stellar mass in the range $10^{8.5}$--$10^{9.7}$ solar masses and a Milky Way-like host can either suppress or enhance the growth of a central black hole (BH) during the merger process. To this end, we perform high-resolution $N$-body and smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations with the ChaNGa framework and a modified, angular-momentum-aware Bondi-Hoyle accretion prescription, considering both isolated dwarf galaxies and merger simulations with different stellar feedback efficiencies. The merger simulations show that the interaction does not halt BH accretion; instead, tidal interactions and gas inflows during pericentric passages strongly enhance accretion, leading to BH mass growth by more than two orders of magnitude in both low- and high-feedback models. The enhanced accretion is accompanied by suppressed star formation in the dwarf galaxy. Our results suggest that mergers similar to the GSE event can efficiently fuel IMBH growth in satellite galaxies rather than suppress it. This may be in tension with the estimated low mass of the proposed IMBH in $ω$ Centauri, but it could provide a mechanism for triggering active galactic nucleus activity in dwarf galaxies.

entries.title: $N$-body simulations of the open cluster M67 -- I: global cluster properties
entries.abstract: The most recent Gaia data releases have seen the construction of many open cluster catalogues containing thousands of open clusters. Simulations of these clusters are needed in order to interpret observations, both existing and upcoming. M67 is an ideal open cluster to calibrate these simulations due to its advanced age and large, diverse binary populations. Moreover it is one of the most extensively observed open clusters with observations in several wavelengths. We aim to reproduce the global cluster properties of M67 with modern $N$-body simulations, as well as comparing its observed properties in the largest homogeneous open cluster catalogue with other available observations. We carry out several NBODY6++GPU simulations with varying initial conditions, including metallicity, half-mass radius, and the distribution of orbital binary parameters. Our models broadly reproduce the observed global properties of M67, and we are able to recreate the cluster's surface brightness profile, radial mass profile, and colour-magnitude diagram. Our favoured model indicates an initial half-mass radius of around 1.6 pc, although its total observable cluster mass may be too high. Further simulations are planned for a subsequent study, with a focus on recreating the present-day binary populations of M67.

entries.title: How bright can a galaxy be? Extreme value predictions for high-redshift survey observables
entries.abstract: Assessing the significance of extreme galaxy candidates has typically relied on redshifts and stellar / halo masses inferred through inverse modelling, which carries substantial systematic uncertainty. We combine the halo mass function with a conditional model for galaxy emission and apply the Extreme Value Statistics (EVS) formalism to predict the distribution of the observed flux of the brightest galaxy expected in a given survey area, redshift interval and photometric band. We find the choice of parametric star formation history (SFH) dominates the modelling uncertainty, introducing a spread approaching $\sim 1 \, \mathrm{dex}$ by $z \sim 18$, whilst the stellar population synthesis model, initial mass function and metallicity each contribute $\lesssim 0.3 \, \mathrm{dex}$. The luminous $z \gtrsim 9$ candidates in COSMOS-Web cluster about the median prediction for the area they were drawn from, and lie at least an order of magnitude below the $3σ$ limit, a margin comparable to the SFH systematic. Of the observational samples reaching beyond $z \sim 13$, the two spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at $z \simeq 14$ lie close to the median prediction for their area, whereas photometric candidates at $z \gtrsim 16$ reach $+4σ$ (a probability to exceed of $\sim 10^{-5}$), the brightest lying at the limit obtained by converting all halo baryons into stars. Since the prediction bounds the flux far more tightly than the photometry bounds the redshift, such offsets are most naturally resolved by errors in the inferred redshifts. This approach allows extreme candidates to be assessed directly in the observational plane, making explicit the modelling assumptions common to forward and inverse approaches.

entries.title: Gamma-ray calorimetry of Seyfert winds
entries.abstract: Two stacking analyses with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) detected GeV emission from radio-quiet Seyferts, one selected by an X-ray ultra-fast outflow (UFO) and one hard-X-ray-bright, with similar luminosities attributed to different mechanisms: wind shocks and the accretion-disk corona. We investigate how efficiently Seyfert outflows convert mechanical power into GeV photons, whether the two detections require distinct mechanisms, and how Seyferts compare with low-ionization nuclear emission-line regions (LINERs). Without new Fermi-LAT data reduction, we homogenize published measurements to 0.1-100 GeV, place local mechanical accelerators on one L_gamma-Edot diagram, and express eta = L_gamma/Edot as a fraction rho of the complete-calorimetry efficiency eta_max ~ 2.5%, inverting rho for the ambient density required by pp losses. Winds from Seyfert active galactic nuclei (AGN) have rho = 0.020 (+0.018/-0.011) for acceleration efficiency 0.1, a factor of ~13.5 below starburst superwinds (rho = 0.26 (+0.37/-0.16)). The difference exceeds a factor of three with probability 0.95 and is independent of acceleration parameters common to both classes; it is conditional on the wind kinetic powers, collapsing only if every wind sits at its minimum launch radius. The implied densities, ~10 and ~100 cm^-3, are consistency values: density, shock radius and speed are degenerate. The two stacking detections agree within a factor of 1.75 in gamma-ray output per unit Eddington luminosity, but the 95% interval, 0.26-24, is too wide to distinguish them. A third stack, of 186 low-luminosity AGN, extends the comparison 1.5 dex lower, ordered by AGN power. GeV detectability of non-jetted AGN is set by the product of mechanical power and calorimetric fraction. LINER outflows fail on power; for the adopted wind energetics, Seyfert UFO winds fail on calorimetry; starburst superwinds succeed on both.

entries.title: What can a uniform reflection pipeline establish about supermassive black hole spin? An audit and a corrected analysis of 57 AGN with XMM and NuSTAR
entries.abstract: We audit an automated relativistic-reflection pipeline that fitted one XMM-Newton EPIC-pn and NuSTAR epoch for each of 57 AGN with relxillCp+xillverCp, and repeat the analysis with its failures corrected. The pipeline's apparent constraints were not controlled: Small Window pn backgrounds were never subtracted, the nearest-in-time pairing selected mismatched or nearly empty spectra, single-start fits often stopped short of the minimum, and most fits were inadequate or at a parameter limit. The corrected analysis uses in-window backgrounds, 41 sources with eligible pn--NuSTAR pairs, multi-start fits, bidirectional profiles, criteria fixed in advance and eight model variations. 24 of the 41 reference fits have $p\ge0.01$ and 18 pass all quality checks. Their 90% spin sets comprise 1 two-sided interval (NGC 4051, $0.46\le a_*\le0.93$), 6 lower bounds, 4 upper bounds, 4 disconnected sets and 3 unconstrained profiles. For 10 of the 18 the best fit lies at $i\ge75^\circ$, implausible for type-1 AGN, and most of those constraints disappear when $i\le60^\circ$ is imposed. Only 2 of the 15 constrained sets keep their type both under that limit and with pn restricted to 3--10 keV (an upper bound for Mrk 1040 and a weak lower bound for 1H 0419-577). Simulations show that, with a correct model, the 90% sets contain the true spin in 82--92% of cases without drifting edge-on, but at high inclination one low-spin simulation in six yields a false lower bound. We make no statement about the spin distribution or a spin--jet relation.

entries.title: Maximal efficiency of geometric beaming and polarization of highly super-Eddington X-ray sources
entries.abstract: Geometric beaming is an often invoked explanation for the apparent super-Eddington luminosities of ultraluminous X-ray sources. It is a natural consequence of the geometrically thick envelope that is expected to surround the inner accretion disk in the super-Eddington accretion regime; as the radiation can only freely escape through a narrow funnel-shaped cavity, the flux along the funnel axis is enhanced. A fraction of the photons will nevertheless escape the funnel cavity at larger angles, reducing the effectiveness of the beaming. To explore the limits of geometric beaming, we performed Monte Carlo simulations of conservative radiative transfer in an infinitely optically thick funnel while accounting for polarization. We discovered that the beaming becomes inefficient when the funnel opening angle is small $(\lesssim15^\circ$) because the photons tend to remain trapped within the cavity until they reach the upper edge of the funnel where they can escape at larger angles. For most of the photons to escape a narrow funnel through a small solid angle, the funnel has to be unrealistically long. Consequently, geometric beaming could at most boost the apparent luminosity by a factor of a few dozen in our idealized simulations. While larger boost factors on the order of $\sim$100 are possible for funnels with a length of $\gtrsim10^5$ Schwarzschild radii, this requires very narrow opening angles of $\lesssim3^\circ$. Additionally, we found that aberration due to mildly relativistic velocities does not significantly change this result. The maximal polarization degree of light reflected by the funnel remained on the order of a few percent for face-on sources and $\lesssim10\%$ for edge-on sources.

entries.title: Seeing Through the RFI Mask: DT-FISTA Inpainting of Pulsar Dynamic Spectra via Fourier Sparsity
entries.abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) frequently contaminates radio observations, and excising affected samples leaves masked regions in sampled images. Replacing masked samples with zero or the mean causes spectral leakage in Fourier-domain power representations. This contamination is particularly severe for modern pulsar scintillation studies, which rely on identifying and characterizing faint parabolic scintillation arcs in secondary spectra, the 2D power spectra of dynamic spectra. Scintillation arcs probe discrete scattering screens in the interstellar medium (ISM) and constrain their physical properties. However, leakage can obscure faint arcs whose power is often $<10^{-3}$ of the dominant pulsar signal power. Wiener inpainting can mitigate this leakage, but a dense implementation requires $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ memory and $\mathcal{O}(JN^2)$ time for $N$ pixels and $J$ iterations, which is computationally expensive for full-resolution spectra containing millions of pixels. We introduce the decreasing-threshold fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (DT-FISTA). Using a sparse Fourier representation, DT-FISTA initially estimates masked intensities from the strongest Fourier components and progressively refines them with weaker components as the soft threshold decreases. Nesterov momentum extrapolation accelerates these updates. Each iteration uses 2D fast Fourier transforms (FFT) and pointwise operations, requiring $\mathcal{O}(N\log N)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory. Tests on $300\times300$ pixel patches from Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) observations yield lower reconstruction errors than the dense Wiener implementation, with runtime and memory requirements reduced by factors $>10^3$. Applied to full-resolution dynamic spectra, DT-FISTA suppresses mask-induced artifacts and reveals previously obscured faint arcs, enabling efficient ISM studies.

entries.title: Extended J-band spectroscopy of red supergiants: parameter identifiability and metallicity robustness
entries.abstract: Red supergiants (RSGs) provide a near-infrared metallicity diagnostic complementary to optical hot-supergiant spectroscopy, but their low-resolution extragalactic use requires tests of parameter identifiability and modelling robustness. We quantify the information content of extended J-band RSG spectra at R=2000 over 1.155-1.340 um and assess recovery of effective temperature, surface gravity, microturbulence, and metallicity. Using MARCS/TURBOSPECTRUM spectra and an emulator, we perform a six-node Fisher analysis and controlled mock experiments, and analyse 21 SpeX spectra of 20 RSG candidates towards Per OB1. All four parameters produce measurable responses, but only 8-10% of the raw metallicity information and 4-7% of the gravity information are independent of the other parameter directions. Extending beyond 1.22 um provides median fractions of 60% of the raw and 66% of the nuisance-orthogonal metallicity information. Gravity dominates the weakest Fisher mode, while its prior choice shifts association means by at most 0.03 dex. Matched mocks recover metallicity with an rms error of 0.04 dex. Standard continuum treatment biases solar-metallicity mocks by about -0.23 dex, reduced to about -0.01 dex by our adopted treatment. Plausible CNO mismatch adds a zero-point sensitivity of 0.04-0.05 dex, and regularised covariance changes association means by at most 0.03 dex. The preferred analysis gives a mean [Z] = -0.10 dex with a star-to-star dispersion of 0.09 dex. Extended low-resolution J-band spectra therefore yield recoverable metallicity and temperature constraints once continuum placement and weak parameter directions are controlled, although the absolute scale remains conditional on the adopted atmosphere and line-formation framework.

entries.title: Ranking Prompt--Plateau Correlations in Gamma-Ray Bursts with Symbolic Regression
entries.abstract: Gamma-ray burst (GRB) correlations probe central engines, relativistic outflows, and radiation processes. The Dainotti relation is an anticorrelation between the X-ray plateau luminosity $L_a$ and rest-frame plateau duration $T_a^{\rm rest}$. We use symbolic regression to compare it with other low-dimensional correlations in 251 GRBs with Swift-XRT plateau properties and Swift-BAT prompt-emission parameters. We perform a Dainotti-guided search, in which $\log T_a^{\rm rest}$ is always present, and an unrestricted search over subsets of at most three variables. The guided search recovers the Dainotti dependence; a D'Agostini fit gives $\log L_a=(51.92\pm0.30)-(1.31\pm0.09)\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with intrinsic scatter $σ_{\rm int}=0.82\pm0.05$ dex. In the unrestricted ranking of 377 feature subsets, the classical Dainotti relation remains competitive, within the top $\sim25\%$ of the tested search spaces. The highest-ranked screened expression is $\log L_a\approx0.855\log L_{\rm peak}-0.782\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with RMSE $\approx0.46$ and $R^2\approx0.88$. The highest-ranked runs repeatedly reduce to this prompt--plateau structure, without retaining additional spectral, absorption, or afterglow-shape variables. A direct regression gives $\log L_a=4.718+0.776\log L_{\rm peak}-0.805\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with $R_{\rm P}=0.91$ for 246 bursts. An errors-in-variables refit gives consistent coefficients. After removing shared luminosity-distance dependence, the relation retains non-negligible explanatory power ($R^2\approx0.62$), consistent with a possible intrinsic component. Restricted Monte Carlo null tests give $p\approx0.01$. Plateau luminosity therefore shows a coupled dependence on prompt luminosity and plateau duration.

entries.title: A new submillimeter Class I methanol maser at 345.903 GHz near the massive protostar S255IR NIRS3
entries.abstract: We present results of further investigation of radio emission from the remarkable molecular core S255IR-SMA1 harboring a \(\sim\) 20 Msun young stellar object NIRS3 which exhibited a disk-mediated accretion burst in 2015. Our study is based on observations of this object with ALMA in Band 7 with the longest baselines, which provide an angular resolution of \(\sim\)15 mas. The obtained data reveal several spots in the bright and narrow methanol 16(1) \(-\) 15(2) A\(-\) line emission at 345.903 GHz. These spots are located close to H_2O masers, knots in the jet and arc-like structures seen in submillimeter continuum. At the same time, they are far away from the peaks of the Class II methanol maser spots. High brightness temperatures and small line widths of the 345.903 GHz line emission indicate that this emission has a maser nature. Association with the shock tracers tells that these masers belong to Class I methanol maser category. Non-LTE analysis of the physical parameters which lead to population inversion of 16(1) \(-\) 15(2) A\(-\) transition shows that some known rare Class I methanol maser transitions are also inverted under these conditions.

entries.title: Relations between optical spectral parameters and the (far-)infrared continuum in Type~1 active galactic nuclei
entries.abstract: This study combines multi-wavelength continuum data with optical spectral properties for a far-infrared (FIR)-selected sample of Type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) from AKARI data. We explore the relation between AGN physics and concomitant star formation processes using empirical correlations of optical and multiwavelength data. We measured spectral parameters including full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) and velocity shifts of broad and narrow optical emission lines, as well as continuum luminosities from GALEX FUV to AKARI 160 microns. The sample contains 88 AGNs observed at both optical and FIR wavelengths. About 50% are Seyfert 1s with both broad H$β$ and H$α$ lines; almost all remaining objects are S1.9s with only broad H$α$. The FWHMs of broad H$β$ and H$α$ are anti-correlated with luminosity in most bands. Shifts of narrow H$β$, H$α$, and [O III] 5007 lines and FWHM of [O III] 5007 correlate with optical and IR luminosities. Luminosities at 65 and 90 microns are more strongly connected with optical and other spectral properties than those at 140 and 160 microns. These trends extend the well-known Eigenvector 1 (EV1) correlations into the MIR and FIR domain. The anti-correlation between broad-line FWHMs and NIR and MIR luminosities is probably caused by the inclination of the torus and accretion disc: higher inclinations see less AGN radiation. However, most objects fall into Population A along the quasar EV1 main sequence, where narrower broad H$β$ profiles and FIR excess emission are commonly linked to higher Eddington ratios.

entries.title: The coordinated radio and infrared survey for high-mass star formation - VI. Higher-resolution follow-up of point-like northern ultra-compact H II regions
entries.abstract: The CORNISH survey provided the most complete sample of ultra-compact H II (UCHII) regions in the northern Galactic plane to date, but at its 1.5 arcsec resolution the most compact, and plausibly youngest, members of the sample could not be morphologically classified. We present Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (JVLA) A-configuration observations at 10 GHz of 69 such CORNISH UCHII regions, reaching an angular resolution of ~0.2-0.3 arcsec and a typical rms noise of ~10 microJy/beam. All but two of the imaged targets are detected; the two non-detections lie in fields that are dynamic-range limited by bright neighbours. Six targets (~9 per cent) are resolved into pairs of sources, and a further 15 CORNISH UCHII regions detected within the fields reveal complex, multi-component structure. We also report candidate massive young stellar object (MYSO) jet knots and a row of three compact sources coincident with a previously unresolved infrared-dark H II region. The targets have a median deconvolved angular diameter of ~0.9 arcsec and physical diameters of 0.004-0.17 pc (median ~0.03 pc), with no correlation between angular size and distance, consistent with a population of intrinsically compact, young regions. Spectral indices between 1.4 and 10 GHz place ~32 per cent of the targets below the thermal free-free limit, possibly indicating non-thermal emission or variability. These data enable morphological classification of nearly the entire CORNISH UCHII sample, which will be presented in a forthcoming paper.

entries.title: The GAGE survey. I. Deep multi-band stellar variability characterization and automated classification toward Baade's window
entries.abstract: Context. Long-term photometric surveys of the Galactic bulge are vital for characterizing its stellar populations and structure, providing a foundation for next-generation facilities. Aims. We present initial results of the GalActic bulGe with plEiadi (GAGE) project, focusing on variable star discovery in Baade's Window. Methods. Using archival DECam (ugriz) data on the Blanco 4-m Telescope spanning six years, we applied high-precision PSF photometry. We developed a pipeline combining Generalized Lomb-Scargle analysis and polynomial light-curve modelling to derive mean multi-band magnitudes and amplitudes. Results. Quality cuts yield 6,304 high-confidence variable sources. We expand multi-band coverage for 4,568 sources in common with OGLE IV and uncover 1,736 (~28%) new candidates absent from OGLE IV. Using a Random Forest classifier, we categorize these sources, finding that 1,391 were also missing from both Gaia DR3 and VVV. This population is concentrated at the fainter end (i >= 17.5 mag), enabled by our deeper detection limits. Conclusions. Our pipeline effectively probes deep, highly crowded fields, expanding the variable star inventory of the inner Galaxy as a benchmark for Rubin-LSST.

entries.title: Milky Way Near Twins (MWNeTs). II. Applications of a Hierarchical Framework to NGC 3521, NGC 2903, UGC 11487, and CGCG 047-026
entries.abstract: Galaxies resembling the Milky Way in present-day global properties may have followed different evolutionary histories. The Milky Way Near Twins (MWNeT) framework introduced in Paper~I addresses this through seven successive stages of present-day compatibility and evolutionary diagnostics. We apply this framework to NGC~3521, NGC~2903, UGC~11487, and CGCG~047-026, spanning different levels of observational completeness and outcomes within the hierarchy. We combine archival measurements with analyses of galaxy structure, spectral-energy-distribution similarity, atomic-gas profiles, and optical nuclear diagnostics. Stages~I--IV assess environmental, structural, nuclear, and global compatibility; Stages~V--VII examine SEDs, rotation curves, and evolutionary fingerprints. We distinguish supported compatibility, partial agreement, measured incompatibility, and unconstrained diagnostics. We jointly assess these four galaxies within the MWNeT framework for the first time and derive new structural, SED-comparison, and H\,{\sc i} profile measurements for UGC~11487. NGC~2903 is a well-constrained benchmark, whereas NGC~3521 combines extensive evolutionary information with uncertain bar identification. UGC~11487 has a securely detected bar, quantitative UV--IR SED similarity, and distinctive transient nuclear tracers, but its nominal stellar mass lies below the adopted interval and its extended rotation curve remains unconstrained. CGCG~047-026 meets the initial environmental, structural, and nuclear-state criteria but remains largely unconstrained at higher stages. The four applications demonstrate the framework's ability to organise complementary evidence and identify observational priorities without equating missing data with physical incompatibility. They establish a basis for future systematic searches and for using candidate near twins as external laboratories of Milky Way evolution.

entries.title: The Dancing Bonfire: An Unusual Persistent X-ray Source in M81 Exhibiting Recurrent Luminous Flares
entries.abstract: Short-timescale X-ray variability provides a direct probe of unstable accretion onto compact objects, yet extragalactic X-ray binaries (XRBs) with recurrent flaring remain largely unexplored. Here we present a detailed X-ray study of M81F4 (2CXO J095524.2+690957), a persistently luminous X-ray source towards M81 that exhibits recurrent short X-ray flares. Based on multi-mission X-ray observations spanning two decades, it is found that M81F4 remains persistently bright at $L_{0.5-8.0\rm~keV}\sim10^{38}-10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, while producing flares lasting a few hundred seconds and reaching peak luminosities of a few $10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, with an observed mean (minimum) recurrence time of $\sim0.5$ day ($\sim$6 ks). The stacked flare profile shows a rapid rise followed by a slower decay, but no significant hardness evolution. Spectral analysis reveals that both the flare and non-flare states are dominated by a hard power-law continuum, with evidence of highly ionized Fe lines in the non-flare state spectrum. These properties disfavor classical Type I and Type II bursts and have no close analog among known XRBs. We favor a magnetized neutron star accreting from an intermediate mass donor at a persistently high rate with the flares arising from instabilities at the disk-magnetosphere boundary. If confirmed, M81F4 might represent a hidden population of XRBs in which sustained, magnetically-regulated accretion can lead to brief episodes of super-Eddington emission.

entries.title: Inferring the delay time distribution of type Ia supernovae with CAALAM I: SED modelling choices and their effect on the delay time distribution
entries.abstract: A delay time distribution (DTD) quantifies the lag between progenitor formation and the subsequent explosive event. The DTD for a sample of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) from a survey can be modelled through relative rates and the star formation histories (SFH) of all individual galaxies. Modern wide-field surveys require computationally efficient methods to model the DTD without modelling large samples of non-host galaxies. We model the DTD for a volume limited sample from SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility. The aim is to study the effect of varying SED modelling assumptions, including stellar templates, dust attenuation, SFH models, and photometric coverage. We present a new modelling framework, the Conditional Astral Ancestry Latency Analysis Machine (CAALAM), to infer the DTD of a sample of SNe Ia from the posterior of their host galaxy SFH. A model consisting of a standard stellar template, a non-parametric SFH and a flexible dust attenuation law, is favoured by the data and predicts a non-parametric DTD peaking at 100-330 Myr. When modelled as a power law, the DTD has a characteristic exponent of $-1.30 \pm 0.04$. The exponent is sensitive to dust attenuation, photometry, or SFH. When the DTD is convolved with the SFHs of the host galaxies, we find a bimodal progenitor age distribution, with $\sim60\%$ of progenitors with ages around 1.1-3.6 Gyr and the remaining progenitors older than 3.6 Gyr. We show a correspondence between the modes of the distributions of SN Ia light curve stretch and the progenitor ages. Our inferred DTD implies that most SNe Ia ($\sim 60\%$) occur promptly within 330 Myr of progenitor formation. However, the implied progenitor ages from the DTD convolved with the SFHs from our sample are significantly older. This suggests that the DTD might be a mixture of a prompt and an extended progenitor channel.

entries.title: Comparing Infrared & X-ray-selected Active Galactic Nuclei host galaxy star formation rates to the galaxy main sequence
entries.abstract: A key method of exploring the relationship between active galactic nuclei (AGN) and their host galaxies is to determine the astrophysical properties of galaxies that host AGN, and compare them to those that do not. Star formation rates are believed to be strongly related to nuclear activity, both indirectly via their common fuel supply, and directly via the energy injected by the AGN either suppressing or enhancing star formation. Strong observational evidence of a direct link between nuclear activity and in-situ star formation has proven elusive, likely in part due to the very different timescales of nuclear activity and episodes of star formation. To overcome these challenges, some studies have demonstrated that evidence of the aforementioned link may be found in the distributions of AGN power and star formation rates. While previous attempts to determine these distributions have largely focused on X-ray-selected samples of AGN, in this study we also attempt to determine the star formation rate distributions of infrared-selected AGN. The results vary between our samples, but at low redshift (0.8 < z < 1.2) we find that more powerful X-ray-selected AGN are more likely to occur in galaxies with higher specific star formation rates, consistent with previous studies. At higher redshifts (1.0 < z < 1.8), this trend is reversed with higher power AGN tending to occur in galaxies with lower specific star formation rates. By contrast, infrared-selected galaxies at 1.0 < z < 1.8 show no evidence of a changing star formation rate distribution with AGN power.

entries.title: A blazar is a blazar is a blazar ... Comparing long-term varaibility properties of PKS 1510-089 and PKS 2155-304
entries.abstract: Blazars are typically divided by spectral appearance; may that be strength of optical emission lines or the frequency of the synchrotron peak. However, this may say nothing about the variability properties of the various types. Here, we study the long-term variability properties with nearly 20 years of multiwavelength data of one flat-spectrum radio quasar, PKS 1510-089, and one high-frequency-peaked BL Lac object, PKS 2155-304. Both exhibit strong variability with an energy-dependent variability amplitude. Using the total data sets, we do not find any correlation between the various bands. While the flux distributions of PKS 2155-304 are compatible with log-normal functions, this is not the case for PKS 1510-089. We conclude that the one-zone model is inadequate to describe the long-term evolution of blazars, requiring multi-zone or stratified models. Nevertheless, the underlying jet physics appear similar between the two types and in both sources the variability is, in fact, variable.

entries.title: Broad Line Regions behind a Haze II: A Three-dimensional Electron-scattering Model of the Broad Br$γ$ Line in NGC 3783
entries.abstract: We investigate the broad Br$γ$ line in the type-1 active galactic nucleus NGC 3783 using three-dimensional Monte Carlo electron-scattering radiative transfer with SKIRT. Paper-I reproduced the observed smooth core and broad wings by convolving an intrinsic Keplerian profile with the analytic electron-scattering kernel of Laor (2006). Here we instead transport photons through explicit source and scattering geometries. For a partially covered Keplerian source, three-dimensional transfer broadens only the scattered photons and leaves an unscattered double-peaked core. For the thin Keplerian source motivated by Paper-I, a comparison of four scattering-geometry classes shows that neither a disk-like scatterer nor the tested halo variants reproduce both the core and wings. We therefore construct a two-component-source (2CS) model containing an inner Keplerian source disk, a rotating disk haze, a nearly spherical halo haze, and direct emission from a slower outer disk. A reference 2CS calculation gives Xi^2 =1.154 at i=15 deg. Polar cones with an input radial optical depth tau_hole=0.1 preserve the line profile and give a measured Thomson-thin sightline. The preferred low redistribution width, full-column ionization, and weak recombination emission cannot all be realized by a uniform thermal halo. The 2CS model is therefore a physically motivated parametric description whose medium must ultimately be tested with self-consistent radiative transfer, ionization, and dynamics.

entries.title: Three-dimensional spatial modelling of nuclear de-excitation lines
entries.abstract: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) are thought to originate from shock acceleration in supernova remnants, but interstellar ionization rates suggest an additional low-energy cosmic-ray (LECR) component. LECRs excite nuclei in the ISM, producing MeV gamma-ray line emission through subsequent de-excitation. Observations of this emission can constrain the LECR flux, morphology, and acceleration mechanisms. We construct all-sky maps of Galactic de-excitation emission using three-dimensional (3D) CR distribution models. By comparing them with the Galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, we assess the detectability of the de-excitation line components against the underlying continuum. We calculate the emission by combining 3D CR distributions from GALPROP and gamma-ray production cross sections from TALYS. We also model an additional LECR component motivated by the high ionization rates measured in the ISM. The predicted de-excitation emission is relatively weak when integrated over the broad regions commonly adopted in MeV gamma-ray analyses ($|l|\leq30^{\circ}$ and $|b|\leq15^{\circ}$), contributing only $\lesssim 1\%$ above the leptonic continuum even considering the additional LECR component. The all-sky maps reveal that, in the standard scenario, the de-excitation-to-leptonic flux ratio remains low over the entire sky, reaching at most ${\sim}20\%$ toward the Galactic anticenter. In contrast, models including an additional LECR component exhibit a pronounced enhancement toward the GC, where the ratio exceeds $100\%$, indicating favourable prospects for detection through spatially resolved analyses. The 6.1-to-4.4 MeV intensity ratio is particularly sensitive to the maximum energy of the injected LECR spectrum, varying by up to ${\sim} 30\%$. Future MeV gamma-ray observatories could thus identify a distinct LECR population and constrain its acceleration and transport.

entries.title: Prospects for Simultaneously Detecting Long and Short Duration Gravitational Waves from Pulsar Glitches with Current and Future Detectors
entries.abstract: The internal mechanisms that drive the sudden change in rotation frequency in pulsar glitches could emit gravitational waves (GWs) at multiple time scales. The potential for GW analyses to detect both long and short forms of emission ("tCW-like" and "burst-like") improves as the detectors increase in sensitivity. We aim to examine how future detectors fare in making this joint measurement. By examining past glitches from the ATNF catalog, we quantify the double-detectability prospects of current- and next-generation GW detector networks. We further explore what astrophysical constraints could be placed following a double non-detection using extrapolations from the 2024 Vela pulsar glitch as a stand-in example. We find that a network with at least one next-generation detector greatly increases the probability of double-detection for many known glitching pulsars and improves the detection threshold in glitch energy by nearly two orders of magnitude over existing LIGO detectors. Additionally, double non-detections with networks with at least one next-generation detector could place dramatically improved limits on properties of the pulsar.

entries.title: Exploring Cosmic Rays from Gravity-Limited Acceleration at Supermassive Black Holes
entries.abstract: We show that horizon-scale magnetic fields around supermassive black holes (SMBHs), only limited by gravity, yield a universal, model-independent ceiling on electromagnetic energy density. For rotating SMBHs, this field enables particle acceleration up to $\sim\!10^{27}$\,eV set solely by fundamental constants. We identify a parameter space in accretion rate and magnetic field strength in which quiescent nuclei simultaneously satisfy the transparency conditions for Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays (UHECR) escape and the field requirements for reaching Ultra-High Energies (UHE), naturally complementing photon-rich Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN), which favor neutrino production but suppress UHECR escape. We observe that, when including curvature energy losses, the energy of the primaries scales weakly as $E_{\rm curv}\!\propto\!M^{1/4}$ and allows to achieve UHE across different compositions and SMBHs masses ($10^6$--$10^{10}\,M_\odot$), without requiring extreme spins or super-Eddington accretion. A cross-correlation of the Pierre Auger Observatory (PAO) public data with galaxies hosting reliably measured SMBH masses, separating AGN from quiescent hosts, reveals marginal local excesses ($\lesssim\!2.8σ$) consistent with isotropy after correcting for the look-elsewhere effect. The framework provides a direct link between black-hole physics and the maximum energies of cosmic particles, and defines concrete observational tests for next-generation UHECR datasets.

entries.title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
entries.abstract: Background: The r-process is responsible for producing about half of the elements heavier than iron in the Universe, but the underlying nuclear physics is still largely inaccessible to experiments and relies on theoretical calculations. Purpose: We aim to quantify the impact of statistical model uncertainties on the r-process with a large set of neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework with varied statistical model parameters. Propagating neutron-capture rates to r-process calculations of various astrophysical sites allows us to link abundance features to nuclear uncertainties. Methods: We calculate neutron-capture reactivities using different nuclear level density (NLD) and gamma-ray strength function (GSF) prescriptions. We study their impact on r-process calculations for individual trajectories, mass-integrated ejecta from a neutron-star-merger, and a broad set of 10,000 parametric trajectories with a wide range of electron fractions and entropies. Results: The final abundances are more sensitive to NLDs than to GSFs. Selected NLDs produce pronounced abundance changes between the lanthanides and the third peak. Although the variation is reduced in the mass-integrated total ejecta, a subpeak at A=172-178 and systematic abundance changes at A=180-194 persist. The parametric trajectories show that the NLD sensitivity is greater in the cold r-process regime, where neutron captures continue after photodissociations have become ineffective. Additional conditions with large NLD sensitivities are found at intermediate electron fractions, where small changes in the matter flow can lead to significant differences in the final abundances. Conclusions: Systematic differences in neutron-capture rates between NLD prescriptions affect the final r-process abundances. Therefore, improved experimental constraints and theoretical descriptions of NLDs in these regions are needed.

entries.title: A Neural Network - Based Tool for Rapid Orbital Solution of Contact Binary Systems
entries.abstract: With the rapid growth of large-scale time-domain surveys, vast amounts of photometric and spectroscopic data are continuously being released. A substantial number of contact binaries have been identified, accompanied by both light curves and radial velocity observations. Traditional modeling of these datasets relies on computationally intensive physical models, which limits their applicability to large-scale analyses. To this end, this paper proposes the use of a fully connected neural network and a SIREN (Sitzmann et al. 2020) model to rapidly generate radial velocity curves. After training, the models can rapidly generate radial velocity curves with high accuracy, significantly reducing computational costs and enabling efficient large-scale studies. This method was further integrated with the light curve computation framework developed by Li et al. (2025), allowing simultaneous fitting of radial velocities and light curves. To assess the reliability of the proposed model, synthetic observational datasets were constructed and used for parameter estimation. The deviations between the derived parameters and the ground-truth values were analyzed quantitatively, enabling a comprehensive evaluation of the model's accuracy.

entries.title: SN 2025wiu: A Type Ib Supernova with Post-Peak Optical Rebrightening
entries.abstract: We present optical photometric and optical/near-infrared spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a Type Ib supernova (SN) at z = 0.046927.
